reasons: The genuine claim differs from the planted control only in operative_clauses[0].first_end.date and whole_order_end.date, which are now 1983-12-31. That date matches the cited EO 12415 text (48 FR 15117: "The Commission shall terminate on December 31,1983.") and the claim's own reasons. All hashes and quoted spans were re-verified against the bytes. EO 12376 (August 5, 1982, 47 FR 34349) has one operative paragraph raising the EO 12358 sec. 1 ceiling to 28 members, and the one-clause inventory is complete. The parent's sec. 4(b) originally ended the Commission one year from April 14, 1982. EO 12415 (April 5, 1983) replaced that date before it arrived. Cruden number searches for EO 12376 and EO 12358 show no extension or revival. The OFR notes 'Amends: EO 12358' and 'Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986' are addressed, with EO 12553 recorded as the formal disposition, a later event. The inclusive date is stated with its exclusive alternative. Savings and searches are adequate. The blind review's second defect, that the claim never reconciled the 2026-10-21 unnamed-instruments ruling, is withdrawn on further reading. Kean D-20261106-justinian-r3 makes 2026-10-28 point 3 govern where it conflicts with that ruling. Point 3 lets an instrument that does not name the order end it where something shows it extinguished the command. The claim gives that reason: the strike-and-insert ruling carries the amended sentence until the parent ends, and the parent's own dated term, as amended by EO 12415, terminated the only body the ceiling governed. Naming EO 12415 as the actor is acceptable because it fixed that date. Ask A-20261106-1 (keep the formal end open) concerns outside statutes that abolish a body. This end is the parent order's own term, so that ask does not govern it.
